weaknesses.summary: Equation (3) is a ratio of residual sums of squares, so closer to 1 means a worse fit, the opposite of the sentence. Equation (5) sums a term that does not depend on its index, so the risk term is identically zero as printed. The skill must keep both the sentence and the formula and must not teach either as a working definition.

The left side carries subscript j and the right side never uses j. Rewriting the summand as A_j would invent a formula the page does not print. As printed the penalty vanishes and the objective collapses to raw assets.

The gold sale in equation (6) settles at Y_{g(i+1)}, the next period's price, and equations (14) to (16) divide the gold purchase by the next period's realized price. The bitcoin sale condition subtracts X at i-1 rather than i. A past-only claim cannot be copied from these lines.

Both branches of the unnumbered bitcoin update start from G_{i-1}. The page prints G, so substituting B would fix a defect the authors printed. The skill must not execute this line as a bitcoin update.

The case labelled with the high gold weight computes with the low one, the low label computes with the high one, and the sale label computes a purchase. All three leave bitcoin unchanged. Following the labels and following the formulas give different trades.

Equation (17) prints the factor as an exponent. With the printed inputs the exponent reading gives about 397 and ordinary compounding gives about 714. Neither is the reported 139.2436. The comparison with the trading result rests on a number the printed formula does not produce.
Equation (18) has no left side and no equals sign, and the section heading prints Difinition. The expression cannot be cited as a definition without adding a symbol the page does not print.

The diamonds print X_{g(i+1)} minus Y_{gi}, then |X_g - Y_g|, three different subscripts on one chart, none of them the g(i) and g(i-1) of equation (6). The chart and the equation are not the same test. Copying either as the rule drops the other.
The diamond prints R^i < R^i. As drawn the test never changes its answer, so the chart does not actually choose between the two shares. The skill must not describe this figure as a decision rule.

Figure 9's bitcoin axis tops out at 0.014 while Table 6 lists the insurance holding as 1.07, and one spike is clipped by the border. Figure 17's cash path ends near 1100 against Table 6's 421.14 for the common type. Figure 18 does agree with the radical column. No chart is promoted to confirmation of the table.

The gold coefficient is 0.8592 in three places and 0.8591 in the memo. The terminal value is $132089.1078 in the summary and section 4.3 but $132089.11 in section 3.4. The missing-value fill uses past prices in the summary and the mean of the neighbouring days in section 3.1. The trader split is credited to beta, gamma, w and q in the body and to lambda in the memo. Each pair is kept; none is averaged.

The sentence follows a range on the authors' own result and names no other strategy. Section 4.1 also points the reader to table 8 where the adjacent table is Table 6. A bounded self-check is not a proof of optimality, and the skill must not copy the "so it is proved" wording as evidence.
